intro: A lesson about the Moon. Tap the Moon and we will begin.
b0: The Moon does not shine by itself. It reflects the light of the Sun, like a mirror.
b1: The Sun always lights one half of the Moon. From Earth we see only part of that bright half.
b2: So the Moon seems to change shape. These shapes are called phases: new moon, first quarter, full moon and last quarter.
b3: The whole circle of phases takes about twenty nine and a half days. That is almost one month.

b4.text: In the Artemis II mission, four astronauts fly around the Moon. The journey takes ten days. In that time the Moon does not finish its circle of phases.
b4.say: In the Artemis two mission, four astronauts fly around the Moon. The journey takes ten days. In that time the Moon does not finish its circle of phases.

q0: First question. Does the Moon shine by itself?
ok0: Correct. The Moon does not shine by itself. It reflects the light of the Sun.
no0: Not quite. The Moon does not shine by itself. It only reflects the light of the Sun, like a mirror reflects a lamp.
q1: Second question. What is the phase called when we see the whole bright Moon?
ok1: Correct. That is the full moon.
no1: It is called the full moon. Then the Sun lights exactly the side of the Moon that we see from Earth.

q2.text: Third question. How many days does the Artemis II journey around the Moon take?
q2.say: Third question. How many days does the Artemis two journey around the Moon take?

no2: The journey takes ten days. That is about one third of the whole circle of Moon phases.
